items.doc: Gary Burton NEA Jazz Master Oral History Interview-1
items.title: Gary Burton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, “I talked to the guys in New York, and talked them into asking you to join the RCA family. We’d like to offer you a contract.”

ctx.x: Sometimes they work for me. Sometimes I’m working for them. Hank Garland kind of discovered me, because he was looking for a vibraphone player to be on a jazz record. He was a Country player, but he was going to make a jazz record, and he imagined the sound of vibes and guitar would be really cool. So there were no vibists in Nashville, but he had heard about me from Boots Randolph, another Nashville musician, who was from Indiana, near where I grew up, and had heard me play and recommended me. So one day I rode…

It sounded fantastic to me, so I announced this to my parents. Phase two is...or phase one maybe...I don’t know what... Now, when it happened... The day I finished school, I loaded up my Volkswagen and drove to Nashville, and Hank helped me go around and find an apartment for the summer, and we started playing together. One of our fans was Chet Atkins, who would come into the club every week or two and hear a set of our little trio that we had. At the end of the summer, Chet showed up and said, “I talked to the…
